intent: Changed: mass from 0.6 to 0.7 kg, following the Integrator's advice after iteration 4 showed that lighter mass cut oval finishes and raised oscillation. Kept the widened 12 mm row at y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel radius, and body unchanged so the race isolates mass. Expected result: oval finish rate back toward 0.5 to 0.7 and steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3, with s-bend and slalom max_error near 0.064 m. I am considering mass 0.8 kg (the iteration 1 best) if 0.7 does not recover the oval. I am not considering sensor-size, track, or body changes at this point.
learning: Compare directly with iteration 1 (mass 0.8, 324.07) and iteration 4 (mass 0.6, 247.82). If the oval finish rate is monotonic in mass (0.3 at 0.6, about 0.5 at 0.7, 0.7 at 0.8), grip is the limit and mass should stay at or above 0.8. If 0.7 matches 0.8, mass has a flat region and the lower-inertia option is open. If 0.7 is worse than 0.6, the result is noise and the design should return to the known best.
rationale: Iteration 4 tested mass 0.6 kg against the iteration 1 best (324.07) and scored 247.82. Oval finish rate fell from 0.70 to 0.30 and oval steering_oscillation rose from 0.26 to 0.32, so the lighter robot is losing grip rather than gaining turn response. This matches the Integrator's rule: when finishes fall while oscillation rises, move mass back toward 0.7 to 0.8 kg. Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.10) and iteration 2 (16 mm sensors) both hurt the oval, so I am keeping the widened 12 mm row and the 0.12 m track. I am taking the Integrator's midpoint, mass 0.7 kg. That is a single-variable step back toward the best-known mass of 0.8 kg, so it tests whether the mass-finish relationship is monotonic and whether 0.7 recovers the oval without the yaw-inertia cost of 0.8. I expect oval finish rate near 0.5 to 0.7 and oscillation at or below about 0.3. If the oval does not recover, the next candidate is mass 0.8 kg, the known best.
